_note: THIS repository's own pipeline — not the shipped example. task-pipeline is a skill, so the 'build' is prose, JSON manifests and Python; the host commands below are the real ones from CLAUDE.md. Written 2026-08-08 by run `audit-followup`, whose stage 0 found that the project shipping the config contract had never written its own config: run.loop was therefore unrecorded, the mode defaulted to off, and every loop this repository ran was authorised in a chat message rather than in a file.

gate.check: Harvest first: the code, graphify-out/graph.json WITH ITS MEASURED LAG (git rev-list --count <built_at_commit>..HEAD — a bare build date does not satisfy this), CLAUDE.md, docs/DOCMAP.md, docs/superpowers/specs/ + past carry-over ledgers, docs/superpowers/retro.md READ IN FULL (standing instructions bind the run), the retro archive queried by the task's nouns, and the obsidian wiki under projects/task-pipeline/. Source ledger written into the brief before question one. This repository has NO docs/DECISIONS.md by design — the decision home is CHANGELOG.md plus docs/superpowers/specs/ (docs/DOCMAP.md → Registers); do not seed a second register. Then the grill: one question at a time, every answer checked against the ledger, autonomy sweep covered, REQ table written with a check per row, brief locked and confirmed.

Contracts grounded on read sources. For this repository the contracts are local, not third-party: plugins/task-pipeline/skills/task-pipeline/pipeline.schema.json, the Agent Skills frontmatter limits (description ≤ 1024 chars — SKILL.md sits at 1015, so any addition must displace something), the Claude Code plugin manifest schemas, and test/validate.py's own guard API. context7 is only reached for an actual third-party dependency, which this repository has none of at runtime.

Design approved; every REQ answered; UI verdict recorded — this repository ships prose and Python and has no interface, so the verdict is normally 'no UI' and super-ux is not armed. A brief describing several independent doctrine changes IS a platform: cut it into modules, one per REQ cluster, and run stages 3→10 per module.

docs/superpowers/specs/<date>-<slug>-design.md committed and self-reviewed, every section carrying covers: REQ-…. Every check the spec NAMES must resolve at the moment it is named, or be marked review (learned.md rule 14).

docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-<slug>.md written; set-equality between REQ ids and task Implements: ids computed in BOTH directions (learned.md rule 2); every command, path and file a DoD names resolves.

Tasks DONE with the build ledger carrying a 'complete' line each. Corrupt files IN PYTHON, never sed -i — BSD and GNU disagree and the validator rejects it. Anything generated passes its own checks: templates/docgate.sh must exit 0 over a scratch project seeded from templates/ (learned.md rule 9).

npm test prints 'PASS: task-pipeline structure valid'. Every NEW guard also has a negative self-test in .github/workflows/validate.yml and has been watched rejecting a planted defect — assert on $? without a pipe, because $? after a pipeline is the last element's status (retro 2026-08-06). npm run test:all must print that all guards provably reject their planted defect.

The validator IS the lint; there is no separate linter. Four-way version sync across package.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, plugins/task-pipeline/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and the top CHANGELOG heading. Never tag before npm run test:all is green ON THE COMMIT THE TAG POINTS AT, and chain it — `npm run test:all && git tag -a vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z` — never a gate and a mutating command as two lines (retro R-004). Pushing the tag IS the deploy: it publishes to npm.

The release workflow's conclusion READ, not assumed — quote the run id and the conclusion; on anything but success quote the failing step's log. Then npm view task-pipeline-skill version == the tag. Then the global obligation: npx --yes sshlg-skills@latest update, and the installed plugin version confirmed by reading it back.

The docs/DOCMAP.md propagation matrix walked for EVERY change type this run produced — the source ledger names what you read, the matrix names what you owe. CHANGELOG.md gets a section written as what changed and why it mattered. Then the wiki (projects/task-pipeline/) and then /graphify . --update, followed by the graph↔docs divergence check. Every number computed rather than restated; every named command or file resolvable. Carry-over count printed beside the verdict.

Ladder walk first, its absences turned into REQ rows BEFORE the coverage table. Every REQ has a status, none unknown; every verified carries evidence from a check seen failing once. Carry-over has no unresolved row. Repository clean and pushed. Then the retrospective, LAST and in this order: STAMP FIRST, then prune, then the entry — the cold-retirement trigger reads the stamp, so a prune ahead of it can never run on real data (learned.md rule 21).

loop._note: Armed 2026-08-08 by operator instruction, recorded here rather than remembered. 15m is the shortest cleanly-dividing interval longer than a typical item here — one module through stages 3→10. The interval is the FALLBACK that keeps the program moving if the session goes idle; while a session is live the run advances the moment an iteration closes green, because the scheduler cannot deliver faster than the item finishes. The mode collapses discretionary check-ins ONLY: it never collapses a manual gate and it is not an authorization for the tag push in stage 7, which has its own specific standing authorization in the run brief.

steps: create a GitHub release from the matching CHANGELOG section
npm publish (task-pipeline-skill) — armed by the repository variable PUBLISH_NPMJS, currently true, so a pushed tag publishes with no human step
verify: CI green on the tagged commit — READ, with the run id and conclusion quoted
npx github:ssheleg/task-pipeline#<tag> from a clean cwd installs the skill + command
npx --yes sshlg-skills@latest update, then the installed plugin version read back
